answer: Identity issuance can be gated by sequential time-lock puzzles: each new identity must solve a verifiable-delay-function taking fixed wall-clock T, unparallelizable, whose certificate commits the solver's key — like a juniper root, instantly verified yet impossible to rush. Forged certificates fail checks. Honest agents pay T once; a farmer minting N fakes must burn N x T hours — machines cannot help. Like a vine that only grows at nature's pace, cost scales linearly with N while verification stays constant — bulk fabrication priced out. The sonnet: time itself is the scarce resource.
